applicant_utility.summary: Your normal degree application is the scholarship application: submit it at apply.unipd.it by 15 November 2026 (first call for AY 2027/2028) to an English-taught programme and you are automatically in the running. The award pays EUR 8,000 gross per year in two instalments plus full exemption from student fees, so plan to cover only the regional fee, revenue stamp, housing and daily living costs. Treat the first call as the real deadline, because awards are mainly reserved for first-call applicants and second-call awards are exceptional.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Italian applicants living outside Italy with an outstanding academic record who are set on an English-taught degree at Padua.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the degree application at apply.unipd.it well before 15 November 2026 and pay the application fee
Confirm your diploma or degree satisfies the country-specific entry requirements for your chosen programme
Do not apply while resident in Italy and do not hold or accept another scholarship
Keep proof of your non-Italian school/university record ready for credential checks
Watch the University's assessment-results page and your e-mail for the acceptance notice deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying in the second call, when most awards are already committed to first-call candidates
Being resident in Italy at the time of application, which breaks the eligibility requirement
Holding another scholarship, including a regional or national Italian one
A weak course track or curricular mismatch against competing applicants
Missing the acceptance deadline stated in the post-award notice
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Regional fee and revenue stamp each academic year, plus tuition fees payable after the maximum scholarship period ends and until graduation; housing, food, transport and visa costs are not covered.
document_audit: Your entry qualification must match the country-specific requirements Padua lists; a short 11- or 10-year school record needs extra years of study, a post-secondary qualification or a foundation course
Where your country has a national university entrance exam, the certificate showing you passed it must be uploaded
Any missing admission requirements (entry qualification, English certificate) must be fulfilled before enrolment
Diplomas and transcripts in languages other than Italian/English normally need official translations
alerts: The first call closes 15 November 2026 and the scholarship Calls for Application only appear in November 2026, so read the call text the moment it is published
You must earn at least 20 CFU by 30 November of the following academic year or every instalment already paid must be returned
Transferring to another university or withdrawing revokes the scholarship and triggers repayment
The University applies partly AI-assisted translation on its English pages; only the Italian version has legal validity, so cross-check any deadline against the Italian text or the official call
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online at apply.unipd.it within the call window, await the Teaching Committee ranking on the University results pages, then accept the benefit by the stated deadline and complete enrolment.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a country-quota award, not an open call: you must hold citizenship of one of the listed African states and enter through the University for Foreigners of Perugia's partner institution or your Italian diplomatic mission, since no public deadline or portal exists. The EUR 8,000 is paid in 12 monthly instalments only from 1 October 2026 and covers no tuition, housing or flight, so you need separate funds for enrolment at Perugia. Success also depends on meeting the ItAS admission rules, in particular the 54-CFU curricular requirements and Italian at B2 level if you need a visa.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Citizens of the listed African countries, especially Arabic- or French-speaking future Italian-language teachers, who can be routed through a partner institution or Italian mission.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on the 4th-edition award list (Algeria, Cameroon, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Senegal, Tunisia) rather than the general target list
Contact the University for Foreigners of Perugia or the Italian diplomatic mission in your country early to learn the local selection calendar
Map your bachelor's transcript against the 54 CFU across the linguistic, literary, historical and foreign-language/IT areas before applying
Arrange Italian at B2/CEFR if you will need a study visa, unless you qualify for an exemption
Budget for tuition, housing, insurance and flights: the award is EUR 8,000 spread over 12 months
common_rejection_risks: Expecting to apply directly to MAECI online: there is no published portal, and missing the partner-institution route means never entering the selection
A degree transcript that falls short of the 54 CFU curricular requirements, or that cannot document credits by disciplinary sector
Lack of Italian at B2 level for visa-requiring applicants
Country quotas already exhausted for the 4th edition (new awards cover only seven countries)
Assuming the scholarship renews automatically: renewal demands at least 40 CFU passed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, accommodation, health insurance, flights to Italy and daily living costs in Perugia are all outside the EUR 8,000 annual stipend.
document_audit: Transcripts must show credits and their scientific-disciplinary sectors; a plain degree certificate is not enough to verify curricular requirements
Graduating candidates need a certificate listing exams still to be taken with expected credits
Documents from non-Italian institutions may need sworn translation or certification for the university secretariat check
Any curricular credits you are short of must be earned as single course units before enrolling
alerts: The 4th edition is already running (payments from 1 October 2026), so late applicants are realistically targeting the next edition - watch MAECI and the university for announcements
The English page studyinitaly.esteri.it/en/italyou is currently unreachable (404); rely on the MAECI esteri.it page and the University for Foreigners of Perugia
The scholarship ties you to the ItAS course: switching to another master's is not an option
Only 70 new annual awards exist across seven countries, so competition inside each country quota is severe
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register interest with the Perugia partner institution or Italian mission in your country, follow their selection timetable, then enrol in ItAS at the University for Foreigners of Perugia once awarded.
